title: Maintenance of Widowed Daughter-in-Law — Section 19 HAMA

content.overview: Section 19 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 provides that a Hindu wife is entitled to be maintained after the death of her husband by her father-in-law. The obligation arises if and only if she is unable to maintain herself from her own earnings or property, or from the estate of her husband, father, mother, or son or daughter. The father-in-law’s obligation ceases if he has no means, or if the daughter-in-law remarries.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Widowed Hindu daughter-in-law? (2) Unable to maintain from listed sources? (3) Father-in-law has means? (4) No remarriage?
content.study:
s. 19 is a limited, residual obligation on the father-in-law. Primary resources of the widow must be exhausted first.

The obligation is personal and ends on remarriage or on the father-in-law’s lack of means.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Who may claim
sections.body: Hindu wife after the death of her husband — widowed daughter-in-law.

sections.heading: Inability condition
sections.body: Unable to maintain herself from own earnings/property or from estate of husband, father, mother, or son/daughter.

sections.heading: Cessation
sections.body: Obligation ceases if father-in-law has no means, or if the daughter-in-law remarries.

sections.heading: Relation to other maintenance
sections.body: Residual to other HAMA and estate-based sources; coordinate with parallel remedies.

examples.title: Residual claim
examples.body: Widow without sufficient own resources or estate support may claim from father-in-law who has means, until remarriage.

hypotheticals.question: Does remarriage end the father-in-law’s obligation under s. 19?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. The obligation ceases when the daughter-in-law remarries.

distinctions.title: s. 19 widowed daughter-in-law vs s. 18 wife
distinctions.left: Claim against father-in-law after husband’s death.
distinctions.right: Claim against husband during his lifetime.

misconceptions.trap: Father-in-law is always primarily liable for the widow’s maintenance.
misconceptions.correction: s. 19 is residual: the widow must be unable to maintain herself from the listed sources first.
